name: storyengine
description: StoryEngine — workspace root. See docs/design/ for the design notes.

scripts.dev: pnpm run dev:deps && pnpm --parallel --filter @storyengine/server --filter @storyengine/client run dev
scripts.dev:deps: tsc -b packages/shared packages/sdk packages/modes/scene packages/modes/freeform packages/modes/assistant
scripts.lint: pnpm run lint:es && pnpm run lint:css

devScriptNote: `dev:deps` builds the packages the watched ones import through `dist` — it was `dev:shared` and built only `shared`, which was already short of `sdk` and became visibly short at P7.0, when the mode stopped being a source import of the server and became a package `mode-loader.ts` resolves at run time. Without it a fresh checkout's `pnpm dev` fails with "Mode package @storyengine/mode-scene could not be loaded" — which is the loader saying exactly the right thing about the wrong situation. `tsc -b` on a project builds its references first, so naming the four is belt and braces rather than four builds.
dependenciesNote: The distribution's mode packages, and the root is where they belong. `mode-loader.ts` resolves each by bare specifier at run time, which needs the package linked somewhere on the server's resolution path; declaring it in `packages/server/package.json` would put it there too and would also make the server's manifest say it depends on a mode, which is the edge docs/design/19-tech-stack.md §10 exists to forbid. The root is the distribution — it is what `pnpm build` builds and what the Dockerfile copies — so this is the honest place to say which modes ship. The image says it a second time, in its own deploy steps, because `pnpm deploy` walks one package's dependency closure and the server's does not include these.
